# DocForge project format

> Generated by DocForge 2.3.0 (project format version 4) for the project "OTNFile".
> Do not edit this file: DocForge rewrites it on every save.

This folder is a DocForge documentation project. DocForge is an app for writing and organizing
Markdown documentation and exports a project as one self-contained HTML document.
This file describes how the project is stored, so tools and AI assistants can read and edit it
without DocForge. Everything below is generated from the DocForge version that saved the project.

Terms: a **project** has **tabs**, every tab has a tree of **entries** (called nodes in the files).
Every entry is one Markdown file.

## Folder layout

```text
<project folder>/
  docforge.config.json   project settings, links, tabs and the entry tree (no content)
  docforge.README.md     this file (generated)
  tabs/
    <tab>/               one folder per tab
      <entry>.md         one file per entry, all flat - the nesting lives in the config
  themes/                *.dftheme - project themes (JSON, edited in DocForge)
  languages/             *.dflang - project syntax highlighting definitions (JSON, edited in DocForge)
```

Tab folders and entry files are named after the tab/entry name:
the characters `< > : " / \ | ? *`, control characters and trailing dots are removed.
Names that collide (case insensitive) within the same scope get ` (2)`, ` (3)`, … appended.
A name with nothing left becomes `Unnamed`. DocForge renames the files when an entry is renamed.

Any other file in the folder (like this one) is ignored when the project is loaded.

## docforge.config.json

```json
{
  "id": "project_…",
  "name": "Project name",
  "settings": {
    "isThemePreset": true,
    "currentThemeId": "theme_…",
    "formatGuide": { "enabled": true, "preferences": "" }
  },
  "languagesStyles": [],
  "links": [],
  "tabs": [
    {
      "id": "tab_…",
      "name": "Documentation",
      "folderName": "Documentation",
      "nodes": [
        {
          "id": "node_…",
          "name": "Getting started",
          "fileName": "Getting started",
          "type": "page",
          "children": []
        }
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `id` | Unique id of the project. Never change it. |
| `name` | Project name, shown as the document title. |
| `settings.isThemePreset` | `true`: `currentThemeId` is a built-in theme. `false`: it is the `id` of a theme in `themes/`. |
| `settings.currentThemeId` | Active theme. Built-in themes: `theme_Dark`, `theme_Light`, `theme_Midnight Blue`, `theme_Solarized`, `theme_Rosé Pine`, `theme_Paper`. |
| `settings.formatGuide` | Settings of this file: `enabled` and the author `preferences`. |
| `languagesStyles` | Project highlight colors for languages. Edited in DocForge, leave as is. |
| `links` | Reference links, see [Reference links](#reference-links). |
| `tabs[]` | Tabs in display order. `folderName` is the folder in `tabs/`. |
| `tabs[].nodes[]` | Entry tree in display order. `children` holds the child entries. |
| `node.fileName` | File name of the entry in its tab folder, without `.md`. |
| `node.type` | Entry type, see [Entry types](#entry-types). Missing = `page`. |
| `node.mergeDescendants` | Only for `merged` entries. Missing = `embed`. |

Ids are a prefix plus random lower case letters and digits (`tab_…`, `node_…`, `link_…`).
They must be unique in the project.

## Entry files

Every entry file starts with a frontmatter block that holds its id and name, followed by the content:

```md
---
id: node_lf3k2def4
name: Getting started
---

# Getting started

Content in Markdown…
```

- `id` must be the same as the `id` of the entry in the config. Without an id, DocForge assigns a new one.
- `name` is the display name and wins over the name in the config. Keep it on one line.
- Everything after the frontmatter is the entry content.
- Entries in the config without a file are kept as empty entries.
- Files that are not in the config are added at the end of their tab (top level).
- Tab folders that are not in the config become new tabs named after the folder.

## Entry types

The `type` of an entry only changes how it shows up in the exported document, never the tree.

| type | Name | Export |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `page` (default) | Page | Own page in the export. Children are own pages. |
| `folder` | Folder | Only groups its children in the navigation. Its content is not exported. |
| `merged` | Merged | Children are shown as sections on this page instead of own pages. |

For `merged` entries `mergeDescendants` decides what happens with the children of the children:

| mergeDescendants | Name | Effect |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `embed` (default) | Include all descendants | Children of children are added to the page as well. |
| `separate` | Keep grandchildren as own entries | Only direct children are merged. Their children move one level up and stay own entries. |

- Inside a merged page the type of a section entry is ignored, except that the content of a
  `folder` entry stays hidden (only its name is shown as a heading).
- Section headings are shifted down by their depth (`#` becomes `##`, …), at most to h4.
- The content of `folder` entries is never exported, so do not put documentation there.

## Markdown

DocForge uses its own Markdown parser. Only the following syntax is supported:

| Syntax | Notes |
|---|---|
| `# Heading` … `#### Heading` | h1 to h4 only. |
| `**bold**`, `*italic*`, `_italic_`, `***both***` | |
| `` `inline code` `` | Highlighted with `` {lang=cpp}`code` ``, see [Properties](#properties). |
| Fenced code blocks | Three or more backticks with an optional language tag, see [Languages](#syntax-highlighting-languages). |
| `- item` / `* item` | Nested with 2 to 4 spaces per level. |
| `1. item` | Ordered lists. |
| `\| a \| b \|` tables | Header row, separator row (`\|---\|---\|`), then body rows. Every row starts and ends with `\|`. `:---` / `:---:` / `---:` in the separator row aligns a column left / center / right. |
| `> quote` | One line per quote. |
| `---` | Horizontal rule, on its own line. |
| `[text](https://…)` | External link, opens in a new tab. |
| `[[slug]]`, `{#anchor}` | Reference links and anchors, see [Reference links](#reference-links). |
| `<!-- comment -->` | Not shown in DocForge and not exported. Can span several lines. Inside code it is normal text. |
| `{...}` above an element | Properties of tables and code blocks, see [Properties](#properties). |

Not supported: raw HTML (it is shown as text, except comments), images, strikethrough, task lists,
underlined (setext) headings and footnotes.

Code blocks:

- ```` ```lang ```` highlights the code with the language `lang`.
- ```` ```diff ```` or ```` ```diff:lang ```` marks lines starting with `+` / `-` as added / removed (optionally highlighted as `lang`).
- Unknown or missing tags show the code without highlighting.

## Properties

Tables and code blocks can get properties in a `{...}` block on its own line(s) **directly above**
the element (no blank line between). The same block inside a comment (`<!-- {...} -->`) works too
and stays invisible in other Markdown viewers. A block that isn't followed by an element is ignored.

````md
{hover=row,col; striped; col 1: hl width=120}
| Name | Value |
|------|------:|
| a    | 1     |

{
  copy
  numbers
  label="Example"
}
```js
const a = 1;
```
````

Syntax:

- Entries are separated by `;` or new lines. Every entry is a list of properties separated by spaces:
  `name` (a switch) or `name=value`. Values with spaces need quotes: `label="My code"`.
- An entry can start with a target, then its properties only apply there:
  `col 1:`, `row 2:`, `cell 2,1:` (row, column). Without a target they apply to the whole element.
- Rows and columns are counted from 0. Row 0 is the table header, column 0 the first column.
- Lists and ranges: `col 0,2`, `row 2-4`, `col 0,2-3`, `cell 1-2,1-2`.
- Anything that isn't valid property syntax (like `{#anchor}` or `{ "json": 1 }`) stays normal text.
  Invalid values are ignored.

Table properties:

| Property | Target | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| `hover=cell,row,col` | table | Highlights the cell / row / column under the mouse, any combination. `hover` alone = `cell`. |
| `striped` | table | Every second body row is a bit brighter. |
| `hl` | row, col, cell | Highlights the row / column / cell. Where highlights cross, it gets brighter. |
| `width=120` | col | Width of the column in px (`120`, `120px`) or percent (`20%`). |
| `line=3` | row, col | Thicker line below the row / right of the column, in px (1 to 10). |
| `align=left\|center\|right` | col, cell | Text alignment. Wins over the separator row. |

Code block properties:

| Property | Effect |
|---|---|
| `copy` | Copy button at the top right. |
| `numbers` | Line numbers (old and new numbers for `diff` blocks). |
| `label="Text"` | Text of the language tag. `label=none` hides the tag. |

Inline code: `` {lang=cpp}`void run()` `` highlights inline code with a language from
[Languages](#syntax-highlighting-languages). The properties stand directly in front of the backticks, without a space.

## Reference links

Links between entries are defined once in `links` in the config and used in the content by their slug.
If a target moves, only the link has to be changed.

| Syntax | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `[[slug]]` | Link, the text is the link's `name`. |
| `[[slug\|Text]]` | Link with custom text. |
| `{#name}` | Anchor in an entry that a link can point to (`a-z`, `0-9`, `-`). |

Link object in `links`:

```json
{ "id": "link_…", "slug": "getting-started", "name": "Getting started",
  "target": { "nodeId": "node_…", "anchor": null }, "refs": [] }
```

- `slug`: lower case letters, digits and single `-`, unique in the project.
- `target.anchor`: `null` for the whole entry, otherwise the name of a `{#name}` anchor in the target entry.
- `refs`: entries that use the link. DocForge recomputes it, an empty array is fine.
- Unknown slugs and links with a missing target are shown as broken links. Code is never scanned for links.

## Syntax highlighting languages

The tag of a code block is matched case insensitive against the name and the aliases of a language.
Project languages are checked first, so they replace a built-in language with the same tag.
Only tags made of letters, digits and `_ # + . -` work, so names with spaces need an alias.

## How to make changes

DocForge reloads the project when files change while it is open. Unsaved changes in DocForge
overwrite the files on the next save, so make external changes while the project is saved.

- **Edit content:** change the Markdown below the frontmatter. Keep the frontmatter as it is.
- **Add an entry at the end of a tab:** create `tabs/<tab folder>/<Name>.md` with a frontmatter
  that only has `name` (or none). DocForge adds it and assigns an id.
- **Add an entry at a specific position or as a child:** create the file with a new unique id in the
  frontmatter and add a node with the same `id`, `name`, `fileName`, `type` and `"children": []`
  at that position in the config tree.
- **Add a tab:** create a folder in `tabs/`, or add a tab with a new id, `name`,
  `folderName` and `nodes` to `tabs` in the config.
- **Rename an entry:** rename the file and change `name` in its frontmatter and `name` and `fileName` in the config.
  If only the file is renamed, the old entry stays (empty) and the file shows up as a new entry.
- **Move or reorder entries:** move the node object in the config tree. The file stays where it is,
  because files are always flat in their tab folder.
- **Move an entry to another tab:** move the file to the other tab folder and the node object to that tab.
- **Delete an entry:** delete the file and remove the node from the config. Move or delete its children
  too, and remove or retarget links that point to it.
- **Link entries:** add a link to `links` and use `[[slug]]` in the content, see [Reference links](#reference-links).

Do not:

- change or reuse ids, or give two entries the same id,
- put other `.md` files into the tab folders (every `.md` file there is an entry),
- edit `*.dftheme`, `*.dflang` and `languagesStyles` by hand, they are written by the DocForge editors,
- edit this file, it is overwritten on every save.
